court: In the High Court of Madras†
case_number: Crl.R.C.(MD) Nos. 142 and 143 of 2018 and Crl.M.P.(MD) Nos. 1932, 1933, 2390 and 2391 of 2018
judgment_text:
[Page 144]

1. Crl.R.C.(MD) No. 142 of 2018 has been filed against the Order, dated 15.12.2017, passed by the Sessions Judge, Kanyakumari District @ Nagercoil in C.A. No. 75/2016 confirming the sentence of Simple Imprisonment for two months and Compensation of Rs. 20,000 being the Cheque amount, imposed on the Petitioner by the learned Judicial Magistrate No. I (Fast Track Court), Nagercoil in S.T.C. No. 346/2015, while Crl.R.C.(MD) No. 143/2018 has been filed against the Order, dated 15.12.2017, passed by the Sessions Judge, Kanyakumari District @ Nagercoil in C.A. No. 74/2016 confirming the sentence of Simple Imprisonment for two months and Compensation of Rs. 25,250 being the Cheque amount, imposed on the Petitioner by the learned Judicial Magistrate No. I, (Fast Track Court), Nagercoil in S.T.C. No. 343/2015.

2. When the matter is taken up today, learned Counsel appearing for the parties submitted that the Compensation of Rs. 20,000 & Rs. 25,250 which is the disputed Cheque amount has been paid by the Petitioner/Accused. However, learned Counsel appearing for the Complainants/the respective 1st Respondent herein, submitted that as mandated under the Negotiable Instruments Act, since Sentence of Imprisonment has been imposed on the Petitioner, being held as a defaulter, the Petitioner has to either undergo the sentence or to pay Compensation, which can be twice the Cheque amount. However, as the Petitioner has paid the Cheque amount to the Complainants, it is submitted that in lieu of Sentence of Imprisonment, any nominal Compensation, that this Court thinks fit, may be awarded to the Complainants, in exercise of its inherent powers, so as to fulfil the mandatory condition prescribed under the Act.

3. This Court heard the submission of the learned Counsel for the Petitioner on the above aspect and perused the materials available on record.

4. On a careful analysis of the materials available in the records and taking into consideration the fact that the matter has been settled between the parties amicably and to give a quietus to the issue and at the same time also fulfilling the mandatory condition imposed under the Act, this Court, in exercise of its powers, thinks fit and proper that a sum of Rs. 2,500 (Rupees Two Thousand Five Hundred only) be awarded as Cost in lieu of sentence imposed in each of the Revision, which would meet the ends of justice.

5. Accordingly, these Revision Petitions are allowed with a direction to the Petitioner to pay a sum of Rs. 2,500 (Rupees Two Thousand Five Hundred only) in each of the revision as Cost to the respective 1st Respondent/Complainant, within a period of four weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this Order.

6. Consequently, connected Miscellaneous Petitions are closed. However, there shall be no order as to Costs.
